subject: C6f render-side: results + 2 cross-owner items (Rust planner 115 MRT; line58 oracle)
body: Changes (uncommitted, render-owned files only): render_pipeline.inc fallback: colour slot bound iff pixelFormat!=0 (Metal default writeMask=15 on unbound slots 2..7 no longer forces extra/inert; unbound slot blend ignored); genericFsSubpass (SPIR-V OpTypeImage Dim=SubpassData scan) gates per-draw MRT snapshot copies (render_encoder.inc). Allocator: every level of a render-target (usage&4) texture gets 64B rows (mipmapped 776x24x10 was 3104B). IOSurface import: unaligned BGRA8 stride -> exact owned shadow; always-on TEGU_IOSURFACE_REFUSED (16). nord2_render_pass line-58 now prints values. New host test gpu/build/c6f-lowering-20261026/ca_backboardd_host_test.py (real QuartzCore AIR, exact c6ec descriptors): downsample_4/narrow_blur_11/home_affordance(std_vert1)/attachment_clear(main RT1) all generic-mrt non-inert; CA-shaped allocations 64B rows; 2-attachment passes accepted+drawn (store Unknown + setColorStoreAction), RT1 untouched; b3a8 import -> nil + trace. ASan+release PASS, 1 PENDING. ITEM A (compute/Rust owner, air_bridge.rs:1729 generic_target_formats): [115,115] (and [80,115]) refused at draw: 'generic plan requires R8/RGBA8/BGRA8/RGBA16F, or two BGRA8 targets'. c6ec has 115,115 blur pipelines. Proposed: admit any 2-target set with each f in {10,70,80,115} (per-target emulation writes one single-format RT per job; n2r computes per-target bpp). Needs Rust rebuild; not edited by me. ITEM B (integration_tests): coreanimation_render_pass_test natural strides 4320/4680 cannot be accepted directly: pinned Mesa 81daea66 src/panfrost/lib/pan_layout.h:164-224 pan_linear_or_tiled_row_align_req returns 64 for arch>=7 RGBA formats and even explicit WSI pitches are refused if misaligned (pan_mod.c ~746). Our allocator/import never produce such textures now (pad / shadow). Please build targets through newTextureWithDescriptor / iosurface import and assert 64B rows + acceptance, and keep hand-made unaligned targets as a refusal case.
